content.text: She sent the gift because she preferred a truce to war. Ibn Kathir's reading is that, having seen the might of Sulayman's armies, she judged that fighting him would bring ruin on her people, so she turned to peaceful means, hoping he would accept a gift or a yearly tribute and leave them alone.

citations.cited_text:
ثم عدلت إلى المهادنة والمصالحة والمسالمة والمخادعة والمصانعة، فقالت:

﴿وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون﴾ أي: سأبعث إليه بهدية تليق به وأنظر ماذا يكون جوابه بعد ذلك، فلعله يقبل ذلك ويكف عنا، أو يضرب علينا خراجا نحمله إليه في كل عام، ونلتزم له بذلك ويترك قتالنا ومحاربتنا.

content.text: She then turned to peace, reconciliation, submission and conciliation, saying: "Indeed, I am going to send to them a gift and see with what the messengers return." That is, she would send him a gift suited to him, and see what his answer would be; perhaps he would accept it and hold back from us, or impose a tribute we would bring him every year.

citations.cited_text: She understood how gift-giving has a good effect on people."

content.text: she understood how gift-giving has a good effect on people.
Her test was to see whether he was a king or a prophet:

citations.cited_text: Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "She said to her people, if he accepts the gift, he is a king, so fight him; but if he does not accept it, he is a Prophet, so follow him."
